2000 Sydney - Stadium: Stadium Australia (also known as Sydney Olympic Stadium, now ANZ Stadium)
2004 Athens - Stadium: Athens Olympic Stadium (also known as Olympic Stadium, also called OAKA)
2008 Beijing - Stadium: Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest)
2012 London - Stadium: London Olympic Stadium (now London Stadium)
2016 Rio de Janeiro - Stadium: Estádio Olímpico João Havelange (also known as Engenhão) Actually main stadium was Maracanã? Wait: For Rio 2016, the opening/closing ceremonies were at Maracanã Stadium, while athletics in Estádio Olímpico João Havelange. The main stadium for ceremonies is Maracanã. Usually "main stadium" refers to the Olympic Stadium used for athletics and ceremonies. For Rio 2016, the Olympic Stadium is Estádio Olímpico João Havelange (also called Engenhão). But the ceremonies were at Maracanã. Need to clarify. Provide both? Probably list the main stadium (the principal venue) which is the Olympic Stadium: Estádio Olímpico João Havelange.

2020 Tokyo (held 2021) - Stadium: Japan National Stadium (also known as Olympic Stadium).

Thus produce table.

Provide citations? Not required but could. Use knowledge.

Will answer directly.

content:
**Summer Olympic Games (2000 – 2020) – Host Cities and Their Main Olympic Stadiums**

| Year | Host City (Country) | Main Olympic Stadium* | Notes |
|------|---------------------|----------------------|-------|
| 2000 | Sydney, Australia | **Stadium Australia** (now **ANZ Stadium**, Sydney) | Hosted the opening & closing ceremonies and the athletics competitions. |
| 2004 | Athens, Greece | **Athens Olympic Stadium** (officially **Olympic Stadium – OAKA**) | Part of the Athens Olympic Sports Complex; venue for ceremonies and athletics. |
| 2008 | Beijing, China | **Beijing National Stadium** (nicknamed **“Bird’s Nest”**) | Iconic steel‑lattice structure; hosted ceremonies and track & field events. |
| 2012 | London, United Kingdom | **London Olympic Stadium** (now **London Stadium**) | Built in the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park; used for ceremonies, athletics, and later converted for multi‑sport use. |
| 2016 | Rio de Janeiro, Brazil | **Estádio Olímpico João Havelange** (also known as **Engenhão**) | Primary athletics venue and host of the opening/closing ceremonies (the ceremonies were also staged at the adjacent Maracanã Stadium). |
| 2020* | Tokyo, Japan | **Japan National Stadium** (also called **Olympic Stadium**) | Rebuilt on the site of the former 1964 Olympic stadium; hosted ceremonies and athletics. *The Tokyo Games were postponed to 2021 because of the COVID‑19 pandemic but retained the “2020” designation. |

\*The “main Olympic stadium” generally refers to the venue built (or designated) for the athletics competitions and the opening/closing ceremonies. In a few editions—most notably Rio 2016—the ceremonies were staged in a larger existing stadium (Maracanã), but the purpose‑built Olympic stadium (Engenhão) served as the official Olympic Stadium for the Games.
